mainTopic: A donkey shared with a נכרי is פטור from בכורה, and whether רבי יהודה permits selling a fetus to a נכרי
overview: The משנה opens מסכת בכורות. It lists five ways a Jew and a נכרי can share a donkey or its fetus: buying, selling, partnership, and two kinds of קבלה (raising an animal for a share of the offspring). In every case the newborn is פטור from בכורה, because the פסוק says 'בישראל' and not others. The גמרא asks why so many cases are needed and explains each one. Selling shows the seller is not penalized. Partnership rejects רבי יהודה, who obligates a partnership with a גוי. The מקבל is listed only as a pair to the נותן, and the נותן shows that the חכמים did not penalize the Jewish owner. The גמרא then quotes a משנה from עבודה זרה: רבי יהודה permits selling a broken animal to a נכרי. It asks whether he would also permit selling a fetus. A proof from our משנה is rejected. A second proof begins from a ברייתא of רבי יהודה about קבלה, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: a donkey shared with a gentile is exempt from firstborn status
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists five cases where a נכרי has a stake in a donkey or its fetus. In every case the firstborn is פטור מן הבכורה, learned from the word 'בישראל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who buys the fetus of a gentile's donkey, or sells his donkey's fetus to a gentile (even though he is not allowed to), or becomes a partner with a gentile, or takes a donkey from a gentile to raise, or gives his donkey to a gentile to raise: in all these cases the donkey is exempt from firstborn status. This is because the verse says 'in Israel,' and not among others.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states the basic rule. If a נכרי owns any part of the donkey or its fetus when it is born, there is no מצוה of פטר חמור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of בכור applies only to firstborns that belong fully to Jews. The source is the פסוק 'הקדשתי לי כל בכור בישראל'. The משנה adds a side note: selling a large animal to a נכרי is forbidden in the first place, yet if someone does it, the animal is still exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Fetus (unborn animal)
A non-Jew
He is not permitted (to sell a large animal to a נכרי)
Receivership: one side raises the animal in exchange for a share of the offspring
Exempt from firstborn obligations

steps.whatToRemember: Any ownership by a נכרי in the mother or the fetus, even partial, removes the obligation of בכורה. The source is 'בישראל'.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אף על פי שאינו רשאי' does not mean the exemption fails. It means selling was forbidden, but once it is done, the exemption still applies.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the opening rule of the whole מסכת. The question of who owns the animal decides whether the מצוה of בכורה applies at all.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הַלּוֹקֵחַ עוּבַּר חֲמוֹרוֹ שֶׁל נָכְרִי,
phrases.english: MISHNA: One who buys the fetus of a gentile's donkey,
and one who sells (his donkey's fetus) to him,
even though he is not permitted (to sell it),
one who partners with him, and one who receives (a donkey) from him (to raise),
and one who gives (his donkey) to him in receivership,
is exempt from firstborn status,
as it is stated: 'in Israel,'
but not among others.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַלּוֹקֵחַ עוּבַּר חֲמוֹרוֹ שֶׁל נָכְרִי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A donkey or fetus partly owned by a נכרי (through purchase, sale, partnership, or קבלה) is פטור מן הבכורה, based on 'בישראל'.

steps.title: Why does the משנה list so many cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs all these examples when they all teach the same principle.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why do I need all of these cases?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה spells out five similar cases. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will explain what each case adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the ruling itself. The question assumes a משנה does not repeat itself for no reason, so each case must teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion on the משנה
All these (cases)
Why do I need it?

phrases.english: GEMARA: Why do I need all these (cases)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the משנה lists so many cases
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point each of the משנה's cases teaches

steps.title: Both buying and selling are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the case of selling must be stated even though buying was already stated. Without it, we might think the seller is penalized and his animal stays obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are all necessary. If the משנה had taught only the buyer, I would have said he is exempt because he is bringing the animal into a state of holiness. But the seller removes it from holiness, so I might say the חכמים should penalize him. The משנה teaches us that he too is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the cases are needed. Buying alone would not teach us the law of selling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer moves the fetus from a נכרי to a Jew, bringing it into Jewish sanctity. That is a good act, so exempting it seems easy. The seller does the opposite, which is even forbidden ('אינו רשאי'). So we might think the חכמים would fine him by keeping the בכורה obligation. The משנה tells us there is no such penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: They are necessary (each case teaches something)
I would have thought (an initial, mistaken assumption)
Sanctity: the status of an animal owned by a Jew
Removes, takes out of (a status)
Let us penalize him (a rabbinic fine)
It teaches us (otherwise)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'הוה אמינא' about a penalty is rejected. The seller is NOT penalized; his donkey is פטור like everyone else's.

phrases.english: They are necessary, for if it had taught (only) a buyer,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא מַיְיתֵי לַהּ לִקְדוּשָּׁה,
phrases.english: I would have said (it is exempt) because he brings it into sanctity,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מוֹכֵר דְּקָא מַפְקַע לַהּ מִקְּדוּשָּׁה —
phrases.english: but a seller, who removes it from sanctity,
I would say: let us penalize him,
(therefore) it teaches us (that he is exempt).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by explaining why both buying and selling are needed
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Selling must be stated separately. Otherwise we might think the חכמים fine the seller by keeping the בכורה obligation, since he removed the animal from sanctity.

steps.title: Why does the משנה list partnership?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case of partnership adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who partners with him: why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה and asks why partnership is listed. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once buying and selling are explained, partnership looks like it adds nothing. A partial share held by a נכרי seems to fit the same principle, so the גמרא asks for its specific purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: One who enters a partnership

phrases.english: And one who partners with him: why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same question, now focused on partnership
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the case of partnership with a נכרי adds

steps.title: Partnership is listed to reject רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The case of partnership is stated to exclude the view of רבי יהודה, who holds that a partnership with a גוי is obligated in בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the view of רבי יהודה, who said a partnership with a gentile is obligated in firstborn status. The משנה teaches us that it is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that partnership is listed because there is a real dispute about it. The משנה rules against רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that a Jew's share in a partnership is enough to obligate the animal in בכורה. Our משנה takes the other side: a share held by a נכרי, even partial, exempts the animal. So the case of partnership is not repetition. It decides a real מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude (an opposing view)
Partnership
Obligated

steps.whatToRemember: Each case in the משנה has a purpose. Selling shows there is no penalty on the seller. Partnership rules against רבי יהודה, who obligates an animal owned in partnership with a גוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the משנה's lists are carefully chosen, often to take a side in a dispute between תנאים.

phrases.english: To exclude (the view) of Rabbi Yehuda, who says:
partnership with a gentile is obligated in firstborn status,
(so) it teaches us that it is exempt from firstborn status.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Partnership is listed to reject רבי יהודה's view that a partnership with a גוי is obligated in בכורה; the משנה holds it is פטור.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need the case of the one who receives?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs the case of the מקבל, a Jew who takes a נכרי's donkey to raise for a share of the babies.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the case of the one who receives, why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going down the list of cases in the משנה. Now it asks why the משנה bothers to mention the מקבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקבל case, the נכרי owns the mother and also has a share in the babies. That is already clearly covered by the principle that any נכרי share makes the animal פטור מן הבכורה. So this case seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: One who receives, here a Jew who takes a נכרי's animal to raise in exchange for a share of its offspring
Why do I need it? This asks why a case or phrase is written at all.

phrases.english: And the one who receives, why do I need it?
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's case of a Jew who takes a donkey from a נכרי to raise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of 'why is this case needed' questions after the partnership case was explained.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new teaching the case of the מקבל adds to the משנה.

steps.title: It is stated only because of its mirror case
steps.stepSummary: The מקבל case teaches nothing new by itself. It is written only because the משנה wanted to teach the opposite case, the נותן לו בקבלה, and lists the two as a pair.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the משנה wants to teach the case of 'one who gives to him in receivership.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that the מקבל case is not needed on its own. The משנה included it only as a partner to the next case, which is the one that really matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a style answer. The משנה likes to present matching cases side by side, so it mentions the easy case (the מקבל) to set up the important one (the נותן). The real חידוש is in the נותן case.

keyTerms.meaning: Receivership: an arrangement where one person raises another's animal in exchange for part of the offspring
To teach or to state, said of what the תנא wants to include in the משנה
Because he wants to: a reason why something was written

phrases.english: Because he wants to teach
phrases.notes: 'He' is the תנא of the משנה.

phrases.english: 'and one who gives to him in receivership.'
phrases.notes: The mirror case: a Jew gives his own donkey to a נכרי to raise.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מקבל case is written only as a stylistic partner to the נותן לו בקבלה case.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need the case of the one who gives in receivership?
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא asks what the נותן לו בקבלה case itself adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the case of the one who gives to him in receivership, why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The previous step said the מקבל was written only because of the נותן case. So now the גמרא asks why the נותן case is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the Jew owns the mother and gives the נכרי a share of the babies. Since a נכרי share exempts the animal, this also looks like it follows the same basic rule. So the גמרא wants to know its special point.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gives his own animal to another, here a נכרי, to raise in exchange for a share of the offspring

phrases.english: And the one who gives to him in receivership, why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows directly from step 7, which made the נותן case the important one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new teaching the case of the נותן לו בקבלה adds.

steps.title: Without it we might think the חכמים penalize the Jewish owner
steps.stepSummary: The case is needed because the mother really belongs to the Jew. We might have thought the חכמים would penalize him by obligating the firstborn, so people would not confuse it with an animal fully his own. The משנה teaches that there is no such penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: since the main animal belongs to the Jew, let us penalize him. Otherwise he might come to confuse it with another animal. So the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the special point of the נותן case. The חכמים did not make a קנס here, even though we might have expected one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that onlookers would see a Jew's own donkey raised by a נכרי. They might then think that any Jewish animal kept by a נכרי is exempt, even when the נכרי has no share at all, and that would be a real פטר חמור. The משנה tells us we do not penalize for this. The נכרי's share in the offspring is enough to exempt it, as with the other cases.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary: introduces why a seemingly extra teaching is needed
It would enter your mind to say: introduces the mistaken first thought (הוה אמינא)
The main animal, meaning the mother itself
Let us penalize him, from קְנָס, a Rabbinic penalty
To get confused or mixed up with something else
It teaches us: introduces the actual חידוש

steps.whatToRemember: Every case in the משנה has a reason. The מקבל is listed only to pair with the נותן. The נותן teaches that the חכמים did not penalize a Jew whose own donkey has a נכרי share in its offspring.

phrases.english: It was necessary. It would enter your mind to say:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְעִיקַּר בְּהֵמָה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הִיא, לִיקְנְסֵיהּ,
phrases.english: since the main animal belongs to the Jew, let us penalize him,
phrases.notes: The penalty would be treating the offspring as a real firstborn.

phrases.english: lest he come to confuse it with another animal,
phrases.notes: The other animal is one given to a נכרי to watch, with no share in the offspring, and that one is obligated.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8. It matches the style of step 3, which also rejected a possible penalty on the Jew.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the mother is the Jew's, the חכמים would penalize him and obligate the firstborn so it is not confused with a Jew's animal that has no נכרי share.
steps.terutzMaskana: No penalty is imposed, and the firstborn is פטור.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The נותן case teaches that there is no קנס, even though the main animal belongs to the Jew.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a real נכרי share in the offspring fully exempts the animal. The חכמים did not add a protective penalty here.

steps.title: A משנה elsewhere: רבי יהודה permits a broken animal, בן בתירא permits a horse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from עבודה זרה about the rule against selling large animals to a נכרי. רבי יהודה permits selling a broken animal, and בן בתירא permits selling a horse.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there, in a משנה: רבי יהודה permits selling a broken animal, and בן בתירא permits selling a horse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה from another מסכת. This is a setup line: it gives the background for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one may not sell a large work animal to a נכרי, out of concern that it will be made to work on שבת. רבי יהודה allows a שבורה because it cannot work anyway. בן בתירא allows a horse because it is used for riding, which is not a Torah-level forbidden labor.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there: quotes a משנה from another place in ש״ס
Permits
A broken or injured animal that cannot do work
Horse, used mainly for riding

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is NOT about בכורה. It is about the separate rule of not selling large animals to a נכרי because of שבת. The גמרא will later connect it to our משנה through the case of selling a donkey's fetus.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן הָתָם: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר בַּשְּׁבוּרָה,
phrases.english: We learned there: Rabbi Yehuda permits with a broken animal,
phrases.notes: Source: משנה in עבודה זרה 14b, about selling to a נכרי.

phrases.english: ben Beteira permits with a horse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the list of cases in the משנה has been fully explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה permits selling a broken large animal to a נכרי, and בן בתירא permits selling a horse.

steps.title: Would רבי יהודה also permit selling a fetus?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a fetus, which cannot work, counts as 'broken' for רבי יהודה. The other possibility is that only a damaged animal counts, while a fetus is in its normal state and will grow up to work.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: what would רבי יהודה say about a fetus? Is his reason for permitting there that the animal is broken, and a fetus is also 'broken'? Or perhaps a broken animal is not in its normal state, but a fetus, since this is its normal state, is not considered broken?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an איבעיא about how far רבי יהודה's rule reaches. It sets up two possible ways to understand his reason, and the next steps try to resolve it (steps 12 and 15).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: what matters is simply that the animal cannot work now, and a fetus cannot work either. Side two: רבי יהודה permits only an animal that is defective, outside its normal condition. A fetus is exactly as it should be and will soon be able to work, so it would still be forbidden to sell.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them: introduces a dilemma with two possible sides, which the גמרא then tries to resolve
Fetus
Or perhaps: introduces the second side of the question
Its normal way or natural state
Broken, meaning unable to work

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא will look to our משנה's case of selling a donkey's fetus to a נכרי to resolve this. That is why the topic comes up here in בכורות.

phrases.aramaic: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: עוּבָּר מָה לִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה?
phrases.english: A question was asked of them: regarding a fetus, what would Rabbi Yehuda say?
Is the reason Rabbi Yehuda permits there

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דִּשְׁבוּרָה, עוּבָּר נָמֵי שָׁבוּר הוּא.
phrases.english: because it is broken, and a fetus too is 'broken'?
phrases.notes: The first side: a fetus also cannot work.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: שְׁבוּרָה לָאו הַיְינוּ אוֹרְחֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Or perhaps: a broken animal, that is not its normal way,
but a fetus, since that is its normal way,
is not considered broken?
phrases.notes: The other side: a fetus will grow up and work, so it doesn't count as defective.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: עוּבָּר מָה לִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds directly on the משנה quoted in step 10 by asking how far רבי יהודה's rule reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה's permission depends on the animal being unable to work now, which would include a fetus, or on its being defective, which would exclude a fetus.

steps.title: Proof attempt from our משנה: selling a fetus is forbidden and רבי יהודה is silent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from our משנה that רבי יהודה does not treat a fetus as 'broken'. The משנה says selling a fetus to a נכרי is not allowed, and רבי יהודה does not argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And one who sells to him [a fetus], even though he is not permitted.' And רבי יהודה does not argue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof from the words of our own משנה to answer the question of step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says that one who sells the fetus of his donkey to a נכרי did something 'not permitted'. If רבי יהודה held that a fetus counts as 'broken' (and so may be sold), he should have argued here. Since no argument of רבי יהודה is recorded, the proof concludes that he agrees a fetus may not be sold.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sells
He is not permitted (the act is forbidden to begin with)
Argues / disagrees

phrases.english: Come and hear:
And one who sells [the fetus] to him [the נכרי],
even though he is not permitted [to do so].
And רבי יהודה does not argue.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: וְהַמּוֹכֵר לוֹ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of step 11 from our משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה does not consider a fetus 'broken', so selling it to a נכרי stays forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: 'והמוכר לו אף על פי שאינו רשאי', with no dissent from רבי יהודה recorded.

steps.title: Rejection: the משנה also records no argument on the partnership cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. The משנה also records no argument from רבי יהודה about partnership, receiving, or giving in קבלה. Would you say he agrees there too?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning: one who partners with him, one who receives from him, and one who gives to him in קבלה, where [an argument] is not taught, would you also say he does not argue?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof of step 12 with a rhetorical question. It shows that the משנה's silence does not mean רבי יהודה agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same משנה lists partnership cases and says they are פטור from בכורה. It records no argument from רבי יהודה there either. Yet we know from a ברייתא (coming soon) that רבי יהודה does obligate בכורה in such cases. So the משנה often leaves out his opinion, and his silence proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning. Turns the questioner's logic against him.
One who enters a partnership
It teaches / it is stated (in the משנה)
So too? Here a rhetorical 'would you really say that?'

steps.confusionAlert: This is phrased as a question, but it is not a real question. It is a rejection: the answer is obviously 'no', and that knocks down the proof.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
one who enters a partnership with him,
and one who receives [an animal] from him,
and one who gives to him in receivership,
where [an argument of רבי יהודה] is not taught,
would you also say that he does not argue?

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof built on רבי יהודה's silence in the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's silence is not evidence. It also omits רבי יהודה's known argument on the partnership cases.

steps.title: He argues even though the משנה does not record it, here too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the rejection. Just as רבי יהודה argues on the partnership cases without the משנה saying so, he may argue about selling a fetus without it being recorded.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he argues and it is not taught. Here too, he argues and it is not taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the result of the rejection. The first proof fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we know רבי יהודה disputes the partnership cases even though the משנה is silent, silence cannot show agreement. So for selling a fetus too, he may hold it is permitted (as a 'broken' animal) and simply not be quoted. This proof does not settle the question of step 11, so step 15 brings a new source.

keyTerms.meaning: He argues, but the משנה does not record it
Here too. Applies the same logic to our case.

phrases.english: Rather, he argues, and it is not taught.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The proof from our משנה fails. רבי יהודה's silence there proves nothing, so the גמרא turns to a new source in step 15 to answer the question of step 11.

steps.title: New proof attempt: רבי יהודה's ruling on receiving and giving animals in קבלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא of רבי יהודה. If a Jew receives an animal from a נכרי and it gives birth, he pays half its value to the כהן. If he gives an animal to a נכרי in קבלה, which is forbidden, he is fined up to ten times its value and gives the full value to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says: one who receives an animal from a נכרי and it gave birth, they assess it at its value, and he gives half its value to the כהן. And one who gives to him in receivership, even though he is not permitted, they fine him up to ten times its value, and he gives all its value to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second proof attempt by quoting a ברייתא of רבי יהודה. It is setting up the next move, where it will draw a conclusion from this ברייתא about the fetus question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, this ברייתא confirms what step 13 assumed: רבי יהודה does obligate בכורה when a Jew and a נכרי share an animal, unlike our משנה. In the first case the Jew owns half, so he redeems half. In the second case רבי יהודה calls giving in קבלה forbidden and fines the Jew to buy out the נכרי's share at up to ten times its value. This is exactly the fine that step 9 said our משנה does not impose.

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the 'known argument' of רבי יהודה that made the rejection in steps 13-14 work. It also gives a new source the גמרא will mine for the fetus question.
